subject: Activation & integration handshake — success criteria, SDK routes, timelines
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@finbridge.com>, Evan Park <evan.park@finbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Activation & integration handshake — success criteria, SDK routes, timelines

Hi Samantha / Evan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap so we have a single checklist to drive the POC activation and the integration run. I captured the things we agreed on and a proposed implementation breakdown below.

High-level success criteria (agreed):
- Generate: consistent end-to-end 95th latency < 450ms for 128-token generations under expected pilot traffic (burst ~20 rps).
- Quality: automated pass rate >= 85% on the shared evaluation prompt set (FinBridge trading prompts v1).
- Reliability: graceful fallback to the small-capacity variant with no more than 1% error rate over 24h during planned load runs.

Evaluation plan (quick):
1) Week 0 (this week): grant test tenant + API keys; baseline smoke tests.
2) Week 1: SDK integration + end-to-end sample flows (generate, chat, embedding for retrieval).
3) Week 2: Load sweep and acceptance run using agreed prompt set; capture latency/cost metrics and failure modes.

Proposed timeline (draft):
- Jul 1–5: access + SDK install + sample flows implemented by FinBridge devs.
- Jul 6: technical kickoff (30–45m) — implementation lead + SRE + FinBridge engineers.
- Jul 7–15: integration dev window (streaming + tool-calling hooks).
- Jul 18–22: acceptance/testing window.

Ownership (Redwood / FinBridge):
- Redwood implementation lead: Marissa Cole — SDK help, streaming examples, acceptance instrumentation.
- Redwood CS (commercial & rollout): Ben Carter — commercial checkpoints, usage reporting.
- Redwood SRE: Jonas Weber — perf/load support and escalation.
- FinBridge integration owner: Evan Park — provisioning access, internal QA, acceptance sign-off.

Implementation specifics we discussed — items we need to confirm before kickoff:
- SDK routes: Node and Python SDKs (we will provide snippets for /v1/generate, /v1/stream, and /v1/embeddings). Please confirm if you prefer an HTTP-only flow or direct gRPC websocket streaming for low-latency flows.
- Streaming: we support chunked server->client streaming; confirm desired client buffer window and reconnect policy.
- Tool calling / function hooks: we recommended a webhook-based callout pattern (Redwood triggers POST to a FinBridge action endpoint) for any long-running downstream actions. Confirm security headers and HMAC scheme your infra requires.
- KV caching / prefix reuse: we can provide a cache advisory to reduce token spend for repeated queries.

Attachments: redwood_sdk-integration-checklist.pdf (integration checklist), draft-matrix.yml (mapping of endpoints -> responsibilities).

Next steps: please reply with a) access request (test tenant emails) b) any scheduling conflicts for Jul 6 10:00am PT (we'll target that time for the kickoff), and c) answers to the small implementation choices above (streaming mode, webhook auth).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

—
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Activation & integration handshake — success criteria, SDK routes, timelines

Neha — thanks for the detailed write-up. This aligns well. A few clarifications from our side before the kickoff: 

1) Access: I created a test service account (dev+redwood@finbridge.com) and will share keys once we confirm which environment (staging or sandbox) you need. We prefer staging for closer parity.
2) Streaming: our primary low-latency path is Node backend using websockets. Can you send a Node streaming example that includes reconnect semantics?
3) Tool calling: we prefer webhook POSTs with an HMAC-SHA256 signature (X-FB-Signature). Can Redwood support a configurable HMAC secret in the tool-calling payloads?
4) Token limits: what do you recommend for token-windowing per connection for streaming to avoid keeping KV cache bloated?

I've attached our initial success-criteria spreadsheet (finbridge-success-criteria.xlsx) — includes the prompt set and acceptance thresholds for scoring. Legal will need a short SOW for sandbox usage (commercial team will prep).

We can do the kickoff Jul 6 at 10am PT — Evan and I are available. Please send calendar invite.

Thanks,
Sam

--
Samantha Li
Head of Product, FinBridge Analytics
samantha.li@finbridge.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Activation & integration handshake — success criteria, SDK routes, timelines

Sam — perfect, thanks for the quick confirmations. Below are the implementation answers and the detailed integration plan we'll cover in the Jul 6 kickoff.

Implementation answers (short):
- Environment: staging is fine. We'll provision a staging tenant for dev+redwood@finbridge.com and generate scoped API keys for the trial.
- Streaming: we will provide a Node websocket sample that includes an exponential backoff reconnect (max 5 retries) and an application-level resume token to avoid re-warming the KV cache.
- Tool calling: yes — we support configurable HMAC-SHA256 headers. We'll include a sample signing flow and a rotation guide in the checklist.
- Token-windowing: recommend a sliding window of 2048 tokens per-connection for your streaming flows; for long sessions we'll suggest periodic checkpointing into a short-lived KV with TTL=30m to avoid unbounded cache growth.

Integration plan (what Redwood will deliver before/at kickoff):
- Deliverables by Jul 5 EOD:
  * Node streaming example repo (examples/node-streaming-reconnect.js)
  * SDK snippets for /v1/generate, /v1/stream, /v1/embeddings (Node + Python)
  * HMAC signing example and webhook verification snippet
  * Instrumentation board for acceptance (Grafana link + sample dashboards)
- API routes mapping we recommend: 
  * POST /v1/generate — single request/response generation
  * WS /v1/stream — streaming tokens/events + resume token header X-Resume-Token
  * POST /v1/embeddings — batch embeddings with async job status
  * POST /v1/toolcall — (Redwood->FinBridge webhook) with HMAC header X-RW-HMAC-SHA256

Owner assignments (concrete contacts):
- Marissa Cole (Redwood) — integration lead, I/O, code review for snippets, triage for SDK issues.
- Ben Carter (Redwood) — commercial liaison and acceptance sign-off facilitator.
- Jonas Weber (Redwood SRE) — will join the kickoff for load/runbook coverage.
- Evan Park (FinBridge) — primary FinBridge integration engineer, will own provisioning and acceptance testing.

Acceptance & runbook highlights:
- We will collect: per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), token count per request, error rates, and function-call success rate.
- Acceptance criteria: see attached FinBridge sheet; we'll instrument and push metrics to a temporary Grafana (read-only link).

Schedule (finalized):
- Jul 5 EOD: Redwood deliverables to your shared Drive.
- Jul 6 10:00am PT: Tech kickoff (30–45m). Meet link: https://meet.redwood.com/meet/finbridge-kickoff-0706
- Jul 7–15: Integration dev window (FinBridge + Redwood support).
- Jul 18–22: Acceptance run and final signoff.

Please confirm: 1) staging tenant email to provision (we will only need dev+redwood@finbridge.com), 2) time holds for Jul 6 (we'll send a calendar invite once confirmed).

Thanks — I'll attach the Node streaming example and the checklist by EOD Jul 5.

—
